call_points.text: No numeric FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management reiterated vehicle finance should converge into profitability by end-FY27.
For the next two quarters, current tax and deferred tax should largely offset; the company will reassess loss utilisation in Q4.
Telematics had its highest quarterly device sales, with depreciation rising as devices are depreciated over two years.
Fuel payments recovery is partial and management is more cautious, giving no timeline for full recovery.
Management sees Delhivery's potential entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance as a positive for the industry, not a near-term threat.
GTV is now reported on a standalone tolling basis after removing the fuelling component.
Gross income for FY26 reached ₹715 Cr, up 55% YoY, driven by strong core and telematics growth.
Adjusted EBITDA for FY26 rose 84% YoY to ₹190 Cr, marking the first full year of positive PAT at ₹160 Cr.
West Asia conflict may cause short-term headwinds and drag on trade movement and transaction revenues.
Adjusted EBITDA for FY26 reached ₹190.14 Cr, growing 84% YoY.
West Asia conflict presents short-term freight movement headwinds impacting transaction revenue.
Ongoing fuel shortage led to temporary suspension of OMC loyalty program.
Operating cash flow for FY26 strengthened to ₹169.43 Cr from ₹58.33 Cr in FY25.
Adjusted cash and cash equivalents stood at ₹1,104.10 Cr at end of FY26.
ESOP charges in P&L are projected at ₹4.01 Cr in Q1 FY27 and ₹3.96 Cr in Q2 FY27.
